title: The Missing Rustle
learning_objectives: Explain how the loud drum hid a quieter sound
Connect listening pauses with the new band rhythm

rights.text_author: GitHub Copilot for Read Oasis (original, AI-authored)

parent_prompts: Before reading: The title is The Missing Rustle; what might make a soft rustling sound in a band?
After page 4: Why did Sam stop completely after hearing the bag between drumbeats?
After reading: How did Sam make room for Mo without changing the paper bag?

pages.text: Sam wanted their band to sound like rain. He could hear his drum, but Mo's soft rustle was missing.

vocabulary.definition: A soft sound like paper or leaves moving.
vocabulary.example: The paper bag makes a little rustle.

pages.text: Mo shook a paper bag beside the big drum. Sam saw it moving, but he could not hear it.
pages.image_alt: Mo shakes the same creased paper bag as Sam strikes the red drum, surrounded by strong curved vibration marks.

pages.text: Sam slowed his drumbeats and listened. Between two beats, he heard a soft rustle from Mo's paper bag.

pages.text: Sam stopped drumming to listen. Mo shook the same paper bag, and Sam could hear its soft rustle.

pages.text: The bag was never silent during their rainy song. Sam's loud drum had hidden it, like talking over someone's whisper.

vocabulary.definition: A very quiet way of speaking.
vocabulary.example: I use a whisper so only you can hear.

pages.text: Sam suggested a pause, a short wait between beats. Then they could hear Mo's bag as well.
pages.image_alt: Sam holds one palm open toward Mo while his other hand holds a drumstick beside the drum.

vocabulary.definition: A short wait before you start again.
vocabulary.example: We pause between taps to hear the bag.

pages.text: They tried their new rhythm, a pattern of sounds. Sam tapped twice, then waited while Mo shook the paper bag.
pages.image_alt: Sam waits with both sticks resting flat on the drum while Mo shakes the same creased paper bag beside him.

vocabulary.definition: A pattern of sounds and quiet spaces.
vocabulary.example: Two taps and a shake make our rhythm.

pages.text: Their band sounded like drops and rustling leaves. Sam enjoyed listening to Mo in the quiet spaces.

quiz.prompt: Why did Sam stop after slowing his drumbeats?

options.text: To let Mo start a new song
To hear the small sound more clearly
To help Mo find another paper bag

quiz.explanation: Page 3 says Sam slowed down and heard a soft rustle between beats. Page 4 says he stopped drumming to listen to the bag.

quiz.prompt: What changed between Sam's first try and their new rhythm?

options.text: The bag changed, not the pauses
Both the bag and the pauses changed
The pauses changed, not the bag

quiz.explanation: Page 2 shows Sam unable to hear the moving bag. Page 4 confirms the same bag can be heard when he stops. Page 7 changes the pauses between drumbeats, not the bag.

quiz.prompt: What helped Sam make the rain music he wanted?

options.text: Leaving room for a quieter band member
Finding a louder sound for every beat
Playing the whole rain song by himself

quiz.explanation: Page 1 introduces rain music with a missing soft rustle. Page 8 resolves this when quiet spaces let Sam hear Mo as part of the rain sound.

quiz.prompt: Tell how Sam solved the missing rustle mystery, from the loud drum to the new rhythm.
quiz.rubric: not yet: names the drum or bag without explaining the missing rustle; with support: links the loud drum to the hidden bag sound after a prompt; independent: explains hearing the rustle between beats, stopping to listen, and adding pauses so both sounds belong.
quiz.explanation: A retell should connect the listening clues to the choice to leave pauses, not claim the bag was repaired.

activities.prompt: Put the listening clues and new band rhythm in order.

items.text: Sam stops to listen to the bag.
Sam cannot hear the moving bag.
Their rhythm leaves space for Mo.
A rustle reaches Sam between drumbeats.

prompts: Why was seeing the bag move not enough to solve the mystery?
What might happen to the rain music if Sam filled every pause with a drumbeat?

off_screen_prompt: With a grown-up, tap your knees while they rustle a paper bag; then leave pauses like Sam did and describe what you hear differently.
